texts.title: The Regent's Hand
texts.body: You are too young to rule, and the house knows it. {regent.name} rules in your name — signs what must be signed, receives whom must be received, decides what you will be told. A regency is a loan of power, and like any loan it accrues interest to the lender.

choices.defer_to_them: Let {regent.name} rule. Learn what a house looks like from the inside.
choices.assert_yourself: Overrule them once, publicly, on something small. Let it be known you can.
choices.learn_at_their_elbow: Sit through every audience and every ledger. Say nothing. Miss nothing.

texts.title: Coming of Age
texts.body: {heir.name} is sixteen. The child who was a liability to hide is now a person with a path to choose, and the choosing — in this house, as in every house — is yours to make first.

choices.send_to_the_academy: The Academy, as the heirs have always gone. Break them among the children of rivals.
choices.keep_them_close: Keep them at your side. Teach them the house from the inside.
choices.grant_them_a_command: Give them a ship. The household will call it early.

texts.title: The Old Blood
texts.body: {grandee.name} of {grandee.house} does not need to say it; the way the greeting is delayed says it. Your house rose. Theirs was always there. Nothing you hold will make that untrue, and they intend you to know it every time you meet.

choices.outwork_them: Let it lie. Work. The old blood never learns to answer that.
choices.answer_the_slight: Answer in the register they respect. Make it a feud.
choices.buy_a_welcome: Find what they want and give it. Be, for a season, almost welcome.

texts.title: The Knife, Turned
texts.body: The attempt failed — a poison tasted, a window that would not open, a servant who talked. Someone reached for your blood, and the trail runs to {plotter.name} of {plotter.house}. The household has gone quiet in the way households do when they have understood that the walls are not as thick as they looked.

choices.scatter_the_seed: Send the children away under other names. Sleep no better.
choices.demand_satisfaction: Name them before every court that will listen.
choices.return_the_knife: Say nothing in public. Begin to arrange their accident.

texts.title: The Plot, Exposed
texts.body: It was supposed to be an accident. It was not, and now {era:the whole capital|the whole court} knows whose purse the knife came from. Yours. There are three ways out of a room like this one.

choices.deny_everything: Deny it until the denial becomes a fact {era:the Senate|the court} agrees to believe.
choices.offer_a_scapegoat: A steward confesses and hangs. The matter closes.
choices.own_it: Own it before the household. Say it would have been deserved.

texts.title: A Will of Their Own
texts.body: {kin.name} has stopped pretending to agree with you. It shows in the small things first — a seat taken without asking, a letter sent to a rival house, a silence at the table where support used to be. Family with ambitions of its own is the oldest danger a house has, and the one it can least afford to answer badly.

choices.indulge_them: Give them some of what they want. End the sulk; feed the appetite.
choices.discipline_them: Remind them, before the household, who is head of it.
choices.send_them_away: A post at the far end of the Reach. Honours, no power.

texts.title: The Kin Who Left
texts.body: {traitor.name} is gone — to {traitor.house}, with your blood in their veins and, by the oldest law, a claim to what your blood holds. The household says the name carefully now, or not at all.

choices.disown_them: Strike the name from the rolls. The claim will not care.
choices.buy_them_back: Gold and a pardon. Blood bought back cannot be trusted again.
choices.end_the_matter: Say nothing in public. Make the problem smaller.

texts.title: The Suit
texts.body: {suitor.name} of {suitor.house} has asked for your hand — formally, through the proper channels, with the house's seal on the letter. A marriage is an alliance, a bloodline, a claim, and occasionally a person; the councils have already priced the first three. Only you can price the fourth.

choices.accept: Accept. Bind the houses; let the heralds call it love.
choices.refuse_kindly: Refuse, with every courtesy the forms allow.
choices.refuse_coldly: Refuse in a way {era:the capital|the court} will enjoy and their house will not forget.
